{{Short description|Quantum}}
The '''quantum Fisher information''' is a central quantity in [[quantum metrology]] and is the quantum analogue of the classical [[Fisher information]].<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last1=Helstrom |first1=C |title=Quantum detection and estimation theory |date=1976 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=0-12-340050-3}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Holevo |first1=Alexander S |title=Probabilistic and statistical aspects of quantum theory |date=1982 |publisher=Scuola Normale Superiore |isbn=978-88-7642-378-9 |edition=2nd English}}</ref><ref name="BraunstenCaves1994">{{cite journal | last1=Braunstein | first1=Samuel L. | last2=Caves | first2=Carlton M. | author-link2=Carlton Caves |title=Statistical distance and the geometry of quantum states | journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] | volume=72 | issue=22 | date=1994-05-30 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.72.3439 | pmid=10056200 | pages=3439–3443| bibcode=1994PhRvL..72.3439B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Braunstein |first1=Samuel L. |last2=Caves |first2=Carlton M. |last3=Milburn |first3=G.J. |author-link2=Carlton Caves |title=Generalized Uncertainty Relations: Theory, Examples, and Lorentz Invariance |journal=[[Annals of Physics]] |date=April 1996 |volume=247 |issue=1 |pages=135–173 |doi=10.1006/aphy.1996.0040|bibcode=1996AnPhy.247..135B |arxiv=quant-ph/9507004 |s2cid=358923 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Paris |first1=Matteo G. A. |title=Quantum Estimation for Quantum Technology|journal=[[International Journal of Quantum Information]] |date=21 November 2011 |volume=07 |issue=supp01 |pages=125–137 |doi=10.1142/S0219749909004839|arxiv=0804.2981 |s2cid=2365312 }}</ref> It is one of the central quantities used to qualify the utility of an input state, especially in Mach–Zehnder (or, equivalently, Ramsey) interferometer-based phase or parameter estimation.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="BraunstenCaves1994" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Wang |first1=Teng-Long |last2=Wu |first2=Ling-Na |last3=Yang |first3=Wen |last4=Jin |first4=Guang-Ri |last5=Lambert |first5=Neill |last6=Nori |first6=Franco |date=2014-06-17 |title=Quantum Fisher information as a signature of the superradiant quantum phase transition |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/16/6/063039 |journal=New Journal of Physics |volume=16 |issue=6 |article-number=063039 |doi=10.1088/1367-2630/16/6/063039 |issn=1367-2630|arxiv=1312.1426 |bibcode=2014NJPh...16f3039W }}</ref>  It is shown that the quantum Fisher information can also be a sensitive probe of a quantum [[phase transition]] (e.g. recognizing the superradiant [[quantum phase transition]] in the [[Dicke model]]<ref name=":1" />). The quantum Fisher information <math> F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,A] </math> of a [[quantum state|state]] <math>\varrho</math> with respect to the [[quantum observable|observable]] <math>A</math> is defined as

:<math>
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,A]=2\sum_{k,l} \frac{(\lambda_k-\lambda_l)^2}{(\lambda_k+\lambda_l)} \vert \langle k \vert A \vert l\rangle \vert^2,
</math>

where <math>\lambda_k</math> and <math>\vert k \rangle</math> are the [[eigenvalues and eigenvectors]] of the density matrix <math>\varrho,</math> respectively, and the summation goes over all <math>k</math> and <math>l</math> such that <math>\lambda_k+\lambda_l>0</math>.

When the observable generates a [[unitarity (physics)|unitary]] transformation of the system with a parameter <math>\theta</math> from initial state <math>\varrho_0</math>,

:<math>\varrho(\theta)=\exp(-iA\theta)\varrho_0\exp(+iA\theta),</math>

the quantum Fisher information constrains the achievable precision in statistical estimation of the parameter <math>\theta</math> via the [[quantum Cramér–Rao bound]] as

:<math>(\Delta \theta)^2 \ge \frac 1 {m F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,A]},</math>

where <math>m</math> is the number of independent repetitions.

It is common to estimate the magnitude of an unknown parameter <math>\theta</math> that controls the strength of a system's Hamiltonian <math>H </math> (i.e. <math>H = A </math>). Optimizing over all states, the maximum quantum Fisher information is given by:<ref name="Giovannetti2006">{{cite journal | last1 = Giovannetti | first1 = Vittorio | last2 = Lloyd | first2 = Seth | last3 = Maccone | first3 = Lorenzo | title = Quantum metrology | journal = Physical Review Letters
 | volume = 96 | article-number = 010401 | year = 2006 | issue = 1 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.010401 | pmid = 16486424 | arxiv = quant-ph/0509179 | bibcode = 2006PhRvL..96a0401G }}</ref><ref name="Zwierz2012">{{cite journal | last1 = Zwierz | first1 = Marcin | last2 = Pérez-Delgado | first2 = Carlos A. | last3 = Kok | first3 = Pieter | title = Ultimate limits to quantum metrology and the meaning of the Heisenberg limit | journal = Physical Review A | volume = 85 | article-number = 042112 | year = 2012 | issue = 4 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.85.042112
| arxiv = 1201.2225 | bibcode = 2012PhRvA..85d2112Z }}</ref><ref name="Giovannetti2011">{{cite journal | last1 = Giovannetti | first1 = Vittorio | last2 = Lloyd | first2 = Seth
 | last3 = Maccone | first3 = Lorenzo | title = Advances in quantum metrology | journal = Nature Photonics | volume = 5 | pages = 222–229 | year = 2011 | issue = 4 | doi = 10.1038/nphoton.2011.35 | arxiv = 1102.2318 | bibcode = 2011NaPho...5..222G }}</ref>
:<math> F_{\rm Q}^{\rm max}[\varrho,H] = (h_{\rm max} - h_{\rm min})^2 </math>,
where <math>h_{\rm max}</math> and <math>h_{\rm min}</math> are the maximum and minimum eigenvalues of <math>H</math> respectively. More generally, for a unitary transform taking time <math>t</math>,
:<math>\varrho(\theta)=\exp(-i t\theta H)\varrho_0\exp(+i t \theta H),</math>
and the quantum Fisher information is bounded by
:<math> F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,H] \leq t^2(h_{\rm max} - h_{\rm min})^2 </math>.
In this case the variance of any unbiased estimate obeys<ref name="Boixo2007">{{cite journal | last1 = Boixo | first1 = Sergio | last2 = Flammia | first2 = Steven T. | last3 = Caves | first3 = Carlton M. | last4 = Geremia | first4 = J. M. | title = Generalized limits for single-parameter quantum estimation | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 98 | article-number = 090401 | year = 2007 | issue = 9 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.090401 | pmid = 17359140 | arxiv = quant-ph/0609179 | bibcode = 2007PhRvL..98i0401B }}</ref><ref name="Pang2014">{{cite journal | last1 = Pang | first1 = Shengshi | last2 = Brun | first2 = Todd A. | title = Quantum metrology for a general Hamiltonian parameter | journal = Physical Review A | volume = 90 | article-number = 022117 | year = 2014 | issue = 2 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevA.90.022117 | arxiv = 1407.6091 | bibcode = 2014PhRvA..90b2117P }}</ref>
:<math>(\Delta \theta)^2 \ge \frac 1 {m t^2(h_{\rm max} - h_{\rm min})^2}.</math>

==Connection with Fisher information==

Classical Fisher information of measuring observable <math>B</math> on density matrix <math>\varrho(\theta)</math> is defined as <math>F[B,\theta]=\sum_b\frac{1}{p(b|\theta)}\left(\frac{\partial p(b|\theta)}{\partial \theta}\right)^2</math>, where <math>p(b|\theta)=\langle b\vert \varrho(\theta)\vert b \rangle</math> is the probability of obtaining outcome <math>b</math> when measuring observable <math>B</math> on the transformed density matrix <math>\varrho(\theta)</math>. <math> b </math> is the eigenvalue corresponding to eigenvector <math> \vert b \rangle</math> of observable <math>B</math>.

Quantum Fisher information is the [[Infimum and supremum|supremum]] of the classical Fisher information over all such observables,<ref>{{cite journal | last=Paris | first=Matteo G. A. | title=Quantum estimation for quantum technology | journal=International Journal of Quantum Information | volume=07 | issue=supp01 | year=2009 | issn=0219-7499 | doi=10.1142/s0219749909004839 | pages=125–137| arxiv=0804.2981 | s2cid=2365312 }}</ref>
:<math>
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,A]=\sup_{B} F[B,\theta].
</math>

==Relation to the symmetric logarithmic derivative==

The quantum Fisher information equals the expectation value of <math>L_{\varrho}^2</math>, where <math>L_{\varrho}</math> is the [[symmetric logarithmic derivative]].

==Equivalent expressions==

For a unitary encoding operation <math>\varrho(\theta)=\exp(-iA\theta)\varrho_0\exp(+iA\theta),</math>, the quantum Fisher information can be computed as an integral,<ref>{{cite journal | last=PARIS | first=MATTEO G. A. | title=Quantum estimation for quantum technology | journal=International Journal of Quantum Information | volume=07 | issue=supp01 | year=2009 | issn=0219-7499 | doi=10.1142/s0219749909004839 | pages=125–137| arxiv=0804.2981 | s2cid=2365312 }}</ref>
:<math>
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,A] = -2\int_0^\infty\text{tr}\left(\exp(-\rho_0 t)[\varrho_0,A] \exp(-\rho_0 t)[\varrho_0,A]\right)\ dt,
</math>
where <math>[\ ,\ ]</math> on the right hand side denotes commutator.
It can be also expressed in terms of [[Kronecker product]] and [[vectorization (mathematics)|vectorization]],<ref>{{cite journal | last=Šafránek | first=Dominik | title=Simple expression for the quantum Fisher information matrix | journal=Physical Review A | volume=97 | issue=4 | date=2018-04-12 | issn=2469-9926 | doi=10.1103/physreva.97.042322 | article-number=042322| arxiv=1801.00945 | bibcode=2018PhRvA..97d2322S }}</ref>
:<math>
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,A] = 2\,\text{vec}([\varrho_0,A])^\dagger\big(\rho_0^*\otimes {\rm I}+{\rm I}\otimes\rho_0\big)^{-1}\text{vec}([\varrho_0,A]),
</math>
where <math>^*</math> denotes [[complex conjugate]], and <math>^\dagger</math> denotes [[conjugate transpose]]. This formula holds for invertible density matrices. For non-invertible density matrices, the inverse above is substituted by the [[Moore–Penrose inverse|Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse]]. Alternatively, one can compute the quantum Fisher information for invertible state <math>\rho_\nu=(1-\nu)\rho_0+\nu\pi</math>, where <math>\pi</math> is any full-rank [[density matrix]], and then perform the limit <math>\nu \rightarrow 0^+</math> to obtain the quantum Fisher information for <math>\rho_0</math>. Density matrix <math>\pi</math> can be, for example, <math>{\rm Identity}/\dim{\mathcal{H}}</math> in a finite-dimensional system, or a thermal state in infinite dimensional systems.

==Generalization and relations to Bures metric and quantum fidelity==

For any differentiable parametrization of the density matrix <math>\varrho(\boldsymbol{\theta})</math> by a vector of parameters <math>\boldsymbol{\theta}=(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)</math>, the quantum Fisher information matrix is defined as
:<math>
F_{\rm Q}^{ij}[\varrho(\boldsymbol{\theta})]=2\sum_{k,l} \frac{\operatorname{Re}(\langle k \vert \partial_{i}\varrho \vert l\rangle \langle l \vert \partial_{j}\varrho \vert k\rangle )}{\lambda_k+\lambda_l},
</math>
where <math>\partial_i</math> denotes [[partial derivative]] with respect to parameter <math>\theta_i</math>. The formula also holds without taking the real part <math>\operatorname{Re}</math>, because the imaginary part leads to an antisymmetric contribution that disappears under the sum. Note that all eigenvalues <math>\lambda_k</math> and eigenvectors <math>\vert k\rangle</math> of the density matrix potentially depend on the vector of parameters <math>\boldsymbol{\theta}</math>.

This definition is identical to four times the [[Bures metric]], up to singular points where the rank of the density matrix changes (those are the points at which <math>\lambda_k+\lambda_l</math> suddenly becomes zero.) Through this relation, it also connects with [[Fidelity of quantum states|quantum fidelity]] <math>F(\varrho,\sigma)=\left(\mathrm{tr}\left[\sqrt{\sqrt{\varrho}\sigma\sqrt{\varrho}}\right]\right)^2</math> of two infinitesimally close states,<ref>{{cite journal | last=Šafránek | first=Dominik | title=Discontinuities of the quantum Fisher information and the Bures metric | journal=Physical Review A | volume=95 | issue=5 | date=2017-05-11 | issn=2469-9926 | doi=10.1103/physreva.95.052320 | article-number=052320| arxiv=1612.04581 | bibcode=2017PhRvA..95e2320S | s2cid=118962619 }}</ref>
:<math>
F(\varrho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}},\varrho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}+d\boldsymbol{\theta}})=1-\frac{1}{4}\sum_{i,j}\Big(F_{\rm Q}^{ij}[\varrho(\boldsymbol{\theta})]+2\!\!\sum_{\lambda_k(\boldsymbol{\theta})=0}\!\!\partial_i\partial_j\lambda_k\Big)d\theta_i d\theta_j+\mathcal{O}(d\theta^3),
</math>
where the inner sum goes over all <math>k</math> at which eigenvalues <math>\lambda_k(\boldsymbol{\theta})=0</math>. The extra term (which is however zero in most applications) can be avoided by taking a symmetric expansion of fidelity,<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Zhou |first1=Sisi|last2=Jiang |first2=Liang |title=An exact correspondence between the quantum Fisher information and the Bures metric |date=18 Oct 2019 |eprint=1910.08473|class=quant-ph }}</ref>
:<math>
F\left(\varrho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}-d\boldsymbol{\theta}/2},\varrho_{\boldsymbol{\theta}+d\boldsymbol{\theta}/2}\right)=1-\frac{1}{4}\sum_{i,j}F_{\rm Q}^{ij}[\varrho(\boldsymbol{\theta})]d\theta_i d\theta_j+\mathcal{O}(d\theta^3).
</math>

For <math>n=1</math> and unitary encoding, the quantum Fisher information matrix reduces to the original definition.

Quantum Fisher information matrix is a part of a wider family of quantum statistical distances.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Jarzyna |first1=M. |title=Geometric Approach to Quantum Statistical Inference |last2=Kołodyński |first2=J. |journal=IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory |date=18 August 2020  |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=367–386 | issn=2641-8770 |doi=10.1109/JSAIT.2020.3017469| arxiv=2008.09129 |bibcode=2020IJSAI...1..367J |s2cid=221245983 }}</ref>

==Relation to fidelity susceptibility==

Assuming that <math>\vert \psi_0(\theta)\rangle</math> is a [[ground state]] of a parameter-dependent non-degenerate Hamiltonian <math>H(\theta)</math>, four times the quantum Fisher information of this state is called fidelity susceptibility, and denoted<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gu |first1=S.-J. |title=Fidelity approach to quantum phase transitions |journal=International Journal of Modern Physics B |date=2010  |volume=24 |number=23 |pages=4371–4458 |doi=10.1142/S0217979210056335| arxiv=0811.3127 |bibcode=2010IJMPB..24.4371G |s2cid=118375103 }}</ref>
:<math>
\chi_F=4F_Q(\vert\psi_0(\theta)\rangle).
</math>
Fidelity susceptibility measures the sensitivity of the ground state to the parameter, and its divergence indicates a quantum phase transition. This is because of the aforementioned connection with fidelity: a diverging quantum Fisher information means that <math>\vert\psi_0(\theta)\rangle</math> and <math>\vert\psi_0(\theta+d\theta)\rangle</math> are orthogonal to each other, for any [[infinitesimal]] change in parameter <math>d\theta</math>, and thus are said to undergo a phase-transition at point <math>\theta</math>.

==Convexity properties==

The quantum Fisher information equals four times the variance for pure states

:<math> F_{\rm Q}[\vert \Psi \rangle,H] = 4 (\Delta H)^2_{\Psi} </math>.

For mixed states, when the probabilities are parameter independent, i.e., when <math> p(\theta)=p </math>, the quantum Fisher information is convex:

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[p \varrho_1(\theta) + (1-p) \varrho_2(\theta) ,H] \le p F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_1(\theta),H]+(1-p)F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_2(\theta),H].</math>

The quantum Fisher information is the largest function that is convex and that equals four times the variance for pure states.
That is, it equals four times the convex roof of the variance<ref name="PRA13_Toth_Petz">{{cite journal |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Petz |first2=Dénes |title=Extremal properties of the variance and the quantum Fisher information |journal=Physical Review A |date=20 March 2013 |volume=87 |issue=3 |article-number=032324 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.87.032324|bibcode=2013PhRvA..87c2324T |arxiv=1109.2831 |s2cid=55088553 }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Yu |first1=Sixia |title=Quantum Fisher Information as the Convex Roof of Variance |date=2013 |eprint=1302.5311|class=quant-ph }}</ref>

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,H] = 4 \inf_{\{p_k,\vert \Psi_k \rangle \}} \sum_k p_k (\Delta H)^2_{\Psi_k},</math>

where the infimum is over all decompositions of the density matrix

:<math>\varrho=\sum_k p_k \vert \Psi_k\rangle \langle \Psi_k \vert. </math>

Note that <math> \vert \Psi_k\rangle </math> are not necessarily orthogonal to each other. The above optimization can be rewritten as an optimization over the two-copy space as <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Moroder |first2=Tobias |last3=Gühne |first3=Otfried |title=Evaluating Convex Roof Entanglement Measures |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=21 April 2015 |volume=114 |issue=16 |article-number=160501 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.160501|pmid=25955038 |arxiv=1409.3806 |bibcode=2015PhRvL.114p0501T |s2cid=39578286 }}</ref>
:<math>
F_Q[\varrho,H]=
\min_{\varrho_{12}} 2{\rm Tr}[(H\otimes {\rm Identity}-{\rm Identity}\otimes H)^2\varrho_{12}],
</math>
such that
<math>\varrho_{12}</math> is a symmetric [[separable state]] and 
:<math> 
{\rm Tr}_1(\varrho_{12})={\rm Tr}_2(\varrho_{12})=\varrho.
</math>
Later the above statement has been proved even for the case of a minimization over general (not necessarily symmetric) separable states.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Pitrik |first2=József |title=Quantum Wasserstein distance based on an optimization over separable states |journal=Quantum |date=16 October 2023 |volume=7 |article-number=1143 |doi=10.22331/q-2023-10-16-1143|arxiv=2209.09925|bibcode=2023Quant...7.1143T |s2cid=252408568 }}</ref> Thus, the minimum of a correlation term is given as
:<math> 
\max_{\varrho_{12}\in {\rm Sep}(\varrho)}\langle H\otimes H\rangle_{\varrho_{12}}=\langle H^2\rangle_{\varrho}-\frac 1 4 F_Q[\varrho,H],
</math>
where <math> {\rm Sep}(\varrho)</math> is the set of bipartite separable states with a marginal <math>\varrho</math>. Here, <math>H</math> can be a Hermitian operator of any dimension. This can be used to give the minimum for separable states for a ferromagnetic Ising [[spin chain]] with a formula containing the quantum Fisher information.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Pitrik |first2=József |title=General method for obtaining the energy minimum of spin Hamiltonians for separable states |date=2026 |class=quant-ph |eprint=2605.03022}}</ref>

When the probabilities are <math> \theta </math>-dependent, an extended-convexity relation has been proved:<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Alipour|first1=S.|last2=Rezakhani|first2=A. T.|date=2015-04-07|title=Extended convexity of quantum Fisher information in quantum metrology|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.91.042104|journal=Physical Review A|language=en|volume=91|issue=4|article-number=042104|arxiv=1403.8033|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.91.042104|bibcode=2015PhRvA..91d2104A|s2cid=124094775 |issn=1050-2947|via=}}</ref>

:<math>F_{\rm Q}\Big[\sum_i p_i(\theta) \varrho_i(\theta)\Big] \le \sum_i p_i(\theta) F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_i(\theta)]+F_{\rm C}[\{p_i(\theta)\}],</math>

where <math>F_{\rm C}[\{p_i(\theta)\}]=\sum_i \frac{\partial_{\theta} p_i(\theta)^2}{p_i(\theta)}</math> is the classical Fisher information associated to the probabilities contributing to the convex decomposition. The first term, in the right hand side of the above inequality, can be considered as the average quantum Fisher information of the density matrices in the convex decomposition.

==Inequalities for composite systems==

We need to understand the behavior of quantum Fisher information in composite system in order to study quantum metrology of many-particle systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Apellaniz |first2=Iagoba |title=Quantum metrology from a quantum information science perspective |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical |date=24 October 2014 |volume=47 |issue=42 |article-number=424006 |doi=10.1088/1751-8113/47/42/424006|bibcode=2014JPhA...47P4006T |arxiv=1405.4878 |s2cid=119261375 }}</ref>
For product states,

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_1 \otimes \varrho_2 , H_1\otimes {\rm Identity}+{\rm Identity} \otimes H_2] =
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_1,H_1]+F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_2,H_2]</math>

holds.

For the reduced state, we have

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_{12}, H_1\otimes {\rm Identity}_2] \ge 
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho_{1}, H_1],</math>

where <math>\varrho_{1}={\rm Tr}_2(\varrho_{12})</math>.

== Relation to entanglement ==
There are strong links between [[quantum metrology]] and [[quantum information science]]. For a multiparticle system of <math>N</math> spin-1/2 particles <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pezzé |first1=Luca |last2=Smerzi |first2=Augusto |title=Entanglement, Nonlinear Dynamics, and the Heisenberg Limit |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=10 March 2009 |volume=102 |issue=10 |article-number=100401 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.100401|pmid=19392092 |bibcode=2009PhRvL.102j0401P |arxiv=0711.4840 |s2cid=13095638 }}</ref>

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho, J_z] \le N </math>

holds for separable states, where

:<math> J_z=\sum_{n=1}^N j_z^{(n)}, </math>

and <math>j_z^{(n)}</math> is a single particle [[angular momentum]] component. The maximum for general quantum states is given by

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho, J_z] \le N^2. </math> 

Hence, [[quantum entanglement]] is needed to reach the maximum precision in quantum metrology. Moreover, for quantum states with an [[entanglement depth]] <math>k</math>,

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho, J_z] \le sk^2 + r^{2} </math>

holds, where <math>s=\lfloor N/k \rfloor </math> is the largest integer smaller than or equal to <math>N/k,</math> and <math>r=N-sk</math> is the remainder from dividing <math>N</math> by <math>k</math>. Hence, a higher and higher levels of [[multipartite entanglement]] is needed to achieve a better and better accuracy in parameter estimation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hyllus|first=Philipp|date=2012|title=Fisher information and multiparticle entanglement|journal=Physical Review A|volume=85|issue=2|article-number=022321|doi=10.1103/physreva.85.022321|arxiv=1006.4366|bibcode=2012PhRvA..85b2321H|s2cid=118652590}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Tóth|first=Géza|date=2012|title=Multipartite entanglement and high-precision metrology|journal=Physical Review A|volume=85|issue=2|article-number=022322|doi=10.1103/physreva.85.022322|arxiv=1006.4368|bibcode=2012PhRvA..85b2322T|s2cid=119110009}}</ref> It is possible to obtain a weaker but simpler bound <ref>{{cite book |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |title=Entanglement detection and quantum metrology in quantum optical systems |date=2021 |publisher=Doctoral Dissertation submitted to the Hungarian Academy of Sciences |location=Budapest |page=68 |url=http://real-d.mtak.hu/1230/7/dc_1593_18_doktori_mu.pdf}}</ref>

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho, J_z] \le Nk. </math>

Hence, a lower bound on the entanglement depth is obtained as

:<math>\frac{F_{\rm Q}[\varrho, J_z]}{N} \le k. </math>

A related concept is the [[quantum metrological gain]], which for a given Hamiltonian is defined as the ratio of the quantum Fisher information of a state and the maximum of the  quantum Fisher information for the same Hamiltonian for separable states

<math>g_{\mathcal H}(\varrho)=\frac{\mathcal F_Q[\varrho,{\mathcal H}]}{\mathcal F_Q^{({\rm sep})}(\mathcal H)},</math>

where the Hamiltonian is 

<math>\mathcal H=h_1+h_2+...+h_N,</math>

and <math>h_n</math> acts on the ''nth'' spin. The metrological gain is defined by an optimization over all local Hamiltonians as

<math>
g(\varrho)=\max_{\mathcal H}g_{\mathcal H}(\varrho).
</math>

==Measuring the Fisher information==

The error propagation formula gives a lower bound on the quantum Fisher information
:<math>
F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,H]\ge \frac{\langle i[H,M] \rangle_{\varrho}^2}{(\Delta M)^2}
</math>,
where <math>M</math> is an operator.
This formula can be used to put a lower bound on the quantum Fisher information from experimental results.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lücke |first1=B. |last2=Scherer |first2=M. |last3=Kruse |first3=J. |last4=Pezzé |first4=L. |last5=Deuretzbacher |first5=F. |last6=Hyllus |first6=P. |last7=Topic |first7=O. |last8=Peise |first8=J. |last9=Ertmer |first9=W. |last10=Arlt |first10=J. |last11=Santos |first11=L. |last12=Smerzi |first12=A. |last13=Klempt |first13=C. |title=Twin Matter Waves for Interferometry Beyond the Classical Limit |journal=Science |date=11 November 2011 |volume=334 |issue=6057 |pages=773–776 |doi=10.1126/science.1208798|pmid=21998255 |arxiv=1204.4102 |bibcode=2011Sci...334..773L }}</ref>
If <math>M</math> equals the symmetric logarithmic derivative then the inequality is saturated.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Escher |first1=B. M. |title=Quantum Noise-to-Sensibility Ratio |date=2012 |class=quant-ph |eprint=1212.2533}}</ref>

For the case of unitary dynamics, the quantum Fisher information is the convex roof of the variance. Based on that, one can obtain lower bounds on it, based on some given operator expectation values using [[semidefinite programming]]. The approach considers an optimization of the two-copy space.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Moroder |first2=Tobias |last3=Gühne |first3=Otfried |title=Evaluating Convex Roof Entanglement Measures |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=21 April 2015 |volume=114 |issue=16 |article-number=160501 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.160501|pmid=25955038 |arxiv=1409.3806 |bibcode=2015PhRvL.114p0501T }}</ref>

There are numerical methods that provide an optimal lower bound for the quantum Fisher information based on the expectation values for some operators, using the theory of Legendre transforms and not semidefinite programming.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Apellaniz |first1=Iagoba |last2=Kleinmann |first2=Matthias |last3=Gühne |first3=Otfried |last4=Tóth |first4=Géza |title=Optimal witnessing of the quantum Fisher information with few measurements |journal=Physical Review A |date=28 March 2017 |volume=95 |issue=3 |article-number=032330 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.95.032330|arxiv=1511.05203 |bibcode=2017PhRvA..95c2330A }}</ref> In some cases, the bounds can even be obtained analytically. For instance, for an <math>N</math>-qubit [[Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger state|Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state]]

:<math>
\frac{F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,J_z]}{N^2}\ge (1-2F_{\rm GHZ})^2,
</math>
where for the fidelity with respect to the GHZ state

:<math>
F_{\rm GHZ}={\rm Tr}(\varrho|{\rm GHZ}\rangle\langle{\rm GHZ}|)\ge1/2
</math>

holds, otherwise the optimal lower bound is zero.  

So far, we discussed bounding the quantum Fisher information for a unitary dynamics. It is also possible to bound the quantum Fisher information for the more general, non-unitary dynamics.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Müller-Rigat |first1=Guillem |last2=Srivastava |first2=Anubhav Kumar |last3=Kurdziałek |first3=Stanisław |last4=Rajchel-Mieldzioć |first4=Grzegorz |last5=Lewenstein |first5=Maciej |last6=Frérot |first6=Irénée |title=Certifying the quantum Fisher information from a given set of mean values: a semidefinite programming approach |journal=Quantum |date=24 October 2023 |volume=7 |article-number=1152 |doi=10.22331/q-2023-10-24-1152|arxiv=2306.12711 |bibcode=2023Quant...7.1152M }}</ref> 
The approach is based on the relation between the fidelity and the quantum Fisher information and that the fidelity can be computed based on semidefinite programming.

For systems in thermal equibirum, the  quantum Fisher information can be obtained from the dynamic susceptibility.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hauke |first1=Philipp |last2=Heyl |first2=Markus |last3=Tagliacozzo |first3=Luca |last4=Zoller |first4=Peter |title=Measuring multipartite entanglement through dynamic susceptibilities |journal=Nature Physics |date=August 2016 |volume=12 |issue=8 |pages=778–782 |doi=10.1038/nphys3700|arxiv=1509.01739 |bibcode=2016NatPh..12..778H }}</ref>

==Relation to the Wigner–Yanase skew information==

The Wigner–Yanase skew information is defined as <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wigner |first1=E. P. |author-link=Eugene Wigner |title=Information Contents of Distributions |last2=Yanase |first2=M. M. |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=1 June 1963 |volume=49 |issue=6 |pages=910–918 |pmc=300031 |doi=10.1073/pnas.49.6.910|pmid=16591109 |bibcode=1963PNAS...49..910W |doi-access=free }}</ref>

:<math>I(\varrho,H)={\rm Tr}(H^2\varrho)-{\rm Tr}(H \sqrt{\varrho} H \sqrt{\varrho}).</math>

It follows that <math>I(\varrho,H)</math> is convex in <math>\varrho.</math>

For the quantum Fisher information and the Wigner–Yanase skew information, the inequality

:<math>F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,H] \ge 4 I(\varrho,H)</math>

holds, where there is an equality for pure states.

==Relation to the variance==

For any decomposition of the density matrix given by <math> p_k  </math> and <math> \vert \Psi_k\rangle </math> the relation <ref name="PRA13_Toth_Petz" />

:<math>(\Delta H)^2 \ge \sum_k p_k (\Delta H)^2_{\Psi_k} \ge \frac1 4 F_{\rm Q}[\varrho,H]</math>

holds, where both inequalities are tight. That is, there is a decomposition for which the second inequality is saturated, which is the same as stating that the quantum Fisher information is the convex roof of the variance over four, discussed above. There is also a decomposition for which the first inequality is saturated, which means that
the variance is its own concave roof <ref name="PRA13_Toth_Petz" />

:<math>(\Delta H)^2 =  \sup_{\{p_k,\vert \Psi_k \rangle \}} \sum_k p_k (\Delta H)^2_{\Psi_k}.</math>

==Uncertainty relations with the quantum Fisher information and the variance==

Knowing that the quantum Fisher information is the convex roof of the variance times four, we obtain the relation <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fröwis |first1=Florian |last2=Schmied |first2=Roman |last3=Gisin |first3=Nicolas |title=Tighter quantum uncertainty relations following from a general probabilistic bound |journal=Physical Review A |date=2 July 2015 |volume=92 |issue=1 |article-number=012102 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.92.012102|arxiv=1409.4440 |bibcode=2015PhRvA..92a2102F |s2cid=58912643 }}</ref>
<math display="block">
(\Delta A)^2 F_Q[\varrho,B] \geq \vert \langle i[A,B]\rangle\vert^2,
</math>
which is stronger than the Heisenberg [[uncertainty relation]]. For a particle of spin-<math>j,</math> the following uncertainty relation holds
<math display="block">
(\Delta J_x)^2+(\Delta J_y)^2+(\Delta J_z)^2\ge j,
</math>
where <math>J_l</math> are angular momentum components. The relation can be strengthened as <ref name="PhysRevResearch21">{{cite journal |last1=Tóth |first1=Géza |last2=Fröwis |first2=Florian |title=Uncertainty relations with the variance and the quantum Fisher information based on convex decompositions of density matrices |journal=Physical Review Research |date=31 January 2022 |volume=4 |issue=1 |article-number=013075 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.013075|arxiv=2109.06893 |bibcode=2022PhRvR...4a3075T |s2cid=237513549 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chiew |first1=Shao-Hen |last2=Gessner |first2=Manuel |title=Improving sum uncertainty relations with the quantum Fisher information |journal=Physical Review Research |date=31 January 2022 |volume=4 |issue=1 |article-number=013076 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevResearch.4.013076|arxiv=2109.06900 |bibcode=2022PhRvR...4a3076C |s2cid=237513883 }}</ref>
<math display="block">
(\Delta J_x)^2+(\Delta J_y)^2+F_Q[\varrho,J_z]/4\ge j.
</math>
